correctness.rationale: The construction is noncircular: G(n) and G(z) are defined solely from the independent Kripke model on N. Induction shows ordinary Kripke truth on N and cofinite modal membership at z. Each G(n) is a theory of its finite successor set, and G(z) is a cofinite truth-set filter; both prove G and K. Induction gives truth of Box^k bottom at n exactly for n<k, hence chi_j belongs to G(z) and is false at n=j. The formula theta=not Box chi_0 belongs to G(z) but fails at z. Therefore the common truth intersection is empty, although bottom is not a G(z) member, violating KRep and any global representing relation. An independent induction establishes eventual truth constancy for all formulas along N, providing a same-carrier Kripke relation for each finite set of formulas. A standalone finite-prefix program returned ALL_CHECKS_OK. Scope and infinity/finite-experiment distinction are explicit.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper poses the concrete question of which weak closure-model operators are representable by Kripke relations and exhibits a multi-letter infinite obstruction. This construction isolates the obstacle to zero propositional variables and a single nonnormal world, while showing all finite observations are Kripke-representable on the same carrier. That finite-versus-global representation boundary is a model-theoretic insight about semantic saturation and filter realization, rather than a renamed instance or a routine finite count. The infinitely many modal constraints are explicitly motivated by the representation condition, and no broad unrelated theorem is asserted.
